explanation: The main character in the Book of Job, a righteous man who endures great trials and losses.
An evil spiritual being who challenges God's authority and accuses Job of causing his own misfortune.
Various difficulties and sufferings that Job experiences to test his faith and loyalty.
Job's ability to remain faithful to God, even when facing severe trials and suffering.
Three individuals (Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar) who visit Job and discuss his situation and theological questions.
Conversations between Job and his friends, where they exchange views on God's justice and human suffering.
God's response to Job's complaint, in which He highlights His power and wisdom, and questions humanity's understanding of justice.
Job's recognition that he cannot understand God's plan and his acceptance of his place in the universe.
The restoration of Job's wealth and blessings after his trials and humility before God.
